video.title: I Built an App the Government Doesn't Want You to See

summary: Chris Koerner builds GovDealFinder, a simple search front end over SAM.gov federal contract listings, using Replit Agent 4 with a Claude-written prompt and the free SAM.gov API, in about four minutes. He adds email alerts for new contracts matching saved filters, SEO blog posts, an eligibility quiz, a generated pitch deck, and publishes on a $12 domain. The pitch: the US government spent $834 billion on contracts last year, about $200 billion is reserved for small businesses, and SAM.gov is clunky. The video is a Replit sponsorship; no revenue or monetisation model is discussed.

tactics.name: Wrap a clunky government data site with a simple front end
steps: Find an ugly but high-traffic public data site (SAM.gov, 2.2M visits/month)
Get a free API key from the source rather than scraping
Ask Claude to turn a three-sentence idea into a detailed build prompt
Paste into Replit Agent 4 and let parallel agents build back end, front end and landing page
Add saved-filter email alerts with a pop-up after first search
Add SEO blog posts and an eligibility quiz
Buy a cheap domain and publish

lessons.lesson: Ugly, hard-to-use public data sites are opportunities for simple paid or lead-gen front ends.

lessons.lesson: Use one AI to write a detailed prompt for another AI builder.
Use official APIs instead of scraping to avoid restrictions.
Saved-search email alerts turn one-time visitors into a list.
Non-coders can ship working web apps in minutes with agentic builders.
